results.title: The andronix Command
results.text:
Run these in **Termux** (not inside the distro):

```bash
# install Debian 13 with the XFCE desktop
andronix install debian --de xfce

# open Debian (same as ./start-debian.sh)
andronix start debian

# open Debian's desktop full screen in Termux:X11
andronix desktop debian

# what's installed, and what you can install
andronix list

# update andronix and every installed distro
andronix update

# save Debian to your phone's storage
andronix backup debian --to storage

# pick a backup and bring it back
andronix restore

# make the desktop lighter
andronix tune debian --profile light

# add a dev pack (python, node, java, go, db)
andronix pack add debian python

# delete Debian
andronix remove debian

# delete a Modded OS edition, by its edition id (installer 2.0.1+)
andronix remove ubuntu-kde

# free the space of leftover downloads (installer 2.0.1+)
andronix clean

# check this phone and what Andronix adjusts for it (installer 2.0.1+)
andronix doctor

# report a failed command to Andronix; shows everything first (installer 2.0.2+)
andronix report

# show the version, e.g. andronix 2.0.0
andronix version

# show help
andronix help
```

results.title: The andronix Command
results.text:
installer 2.0.1+

```bash
andronix clean
```

Empties the download cache (`~/.andronix/cache`), for example a download left behind when an install stopped halfway, and prints how much space it freed. Your installed distros aren't touched. A download that's still running is kept.

You rarely need it: a finished install deletes its download, and `andronix remove` deletes the distro's leftover downloads.

results.title: Uninstall a Distro in Termux
results.text: Open the Andronix app and tap the **Linux distros** card on Home.

results.title: The andronix Command
results.text:
The Andronix app (10.0 or newer) sets up `andronix` for you with its install command. Without the app, this one line downloads `andronix`, checks it, and runs an install:

```bash copy
(curl -fsSL --retry 4 --retry-delay 3 https://dl.andronix.app/get.sh -o $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh || curl -4 -fsSL --retry 2 --retry-delay 3 https://dl.andronix.app/get.sh -o $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh) && sh $PREFIX/tmp/get.sh install debian --de xfce
```

Replace `debian` and `xfce` with the distro and desktop you want. After that, `andronix` is installed in Termux and you can use it directly. If Termux doesn't have `proot` yet, the installer installs it first. See [Install without the app](/termux/without-the-app).

`andronix update` keeps it up to date.

results.title: Upgrading from an Older Modded OS
results.section: Removing a Modded OS from Andronix 2.0
results.text: For a Modded OS you installed with Andronix 2.0, use its edition id, for example `andronix remove ubuntu-kde`. See [Remove a Modded OS](/modded-os/modded-os-installation#remove-a-modded-os). To keep its files, back it up first with `andronix backup ubuntu-kde --to storage` ([Back up and restore](/use/backups)).

results.title: Requirements for Termux
results.text:
This page is for Andronix with Termux, on phones that can't run Linux in the app (Android 7, or no 64-bit ARM processor). For everything else, see [Requirements](/start-here/requirements).

In Termux, Andronix runs on more devices than in the app, including Android 7, 32-bit ARM, x86 and x86_64:

| | Command line only | With a desktop |
|---|---|---|
| **Android** | 7 or newer | 7 or newer |
| **CPU** | arm64 (most phones), also arm, x86 and x86_64 for some distros | Same |
| **Free storage** | about 0.5 GB | 1.5 to 2 GB (about 3 GB for KDE Plasma) |
| **RAM** | 2 GB | 3 GB or more is comfortable; 4 GB or more for KDE Plasma |
| **Root** | Not needed | Not needed |

results.title: Requirements
results.text: Andronix runs Linux in the app on most Android phones and tablets from the last several years. Check these before you install.

results.title: Limitations
results.text:
Distros you install in the app have the same proot limits as above, plus:

- **One distro runs at a time.**
- **No microphone** yet; sound output works.
- **No backup inside the app** yet. See [Back up and restore](/use/backups).
- **No VNC from another device.** The desktop shows in the app only. In Termux, [VNC](/termux/vnc) still works.
- **SSH isn't supported** in 10.1. See [SSH](/termux/ssh).
- **arm64 with Android 8 or newer only**; other devices use Termux. See [Requirements](/start-here/requirements).

results.title: Requirements for Termux
results.text: On phones with **less than 3 GB of RAM**, Andronix sets up the desktop with a light profile automatically (no effects, fewer background apps). See [Make it faster](/use/performance). KDE Plasma needs **4 GB or more**; the installer warns you below that.

results.title: Requirements for Termux
results.text: Most phones are **arm64**, and every distro supports it. Some distros also run on 32-bit arm, x86 and x86_64 devices (like Chromebooks); see [Supported distros](/reference/distros). You don't need to check this yourself: the installer checks your CPU first and tells you if a distro doesn't support it.
